newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says no racism debate in Australia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says no racism debate in Australia.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday he did not believe there was a racism debate occuring in Australia.

"I think the claims that have been made by many people in recent days about a racism debate in the Australian community are superficial and juvenile," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio. "I don't think there's a raging racist debate in the Australian community at all."
Howard was responding to independent politician Pauline Hanson's comments on Sunday that Australia faced civil war if migrants and Aborigines continued to get special treatment.

"(The racism debate) is an argument that some people would like to see occur," Howard said. "I find it very strange that people should be beating up the existence of an argument of which there's no evidence to me and to most people I've talked to that there's any such debate around."
Hanson's first speech to parliament, in which she criticised the government over the number of Asians in Australia, sparked widespread community response.
A recent opinion poll published in The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper found 48 percent of respondents backed Hanson, while only 38 percent disagreed with her views.
Howard said he believed the majority of Australians were not racist. "Most Australians are very tolerant," he said.

"... In reality the great majority of Australians have demonstrated a capacity to absorb people from all around the world the like of which few other countries have achieved since the end of World War Two," he said.
"That should be a source of pride - it should not be a source of defensiveness."
